all_of: a reverse proxy fronts one or more applications and selects them by the host header
some reachable endpoint reflects request metadata back to the caller
any_of: an endpoint mirrors the request headers as a structured response
a second application is served only under a host name that is not yet known
a parameter causes the server itself to fetch a url the caller supplies

chain.action: treat a site that looks entirely static as unenumerated, and repeat directory discovery with a wordlist an order of magnitude larger before concluding it is empty
chain.why: the small default wordlist returned nothing here while the medium one found the only dynamic route on its first pass

chain.action: establish exactly which paths the proxy forwards and whether it rewrites them, using the framework's own not-found message as an oracle for the path the backend received
chain.why: the not-found text repeats the backend path verbatim, which settles prefix-stripping and traversal questions without guessing

chain.action: send the reflecting endpoint a request with the protocol version that makes the host header optional, and omit that header entirely
chain.why: the proxy then serves its default virtual host, and the reflection prints that host name, disclosing the internal domain the rest of the application is keyed on

chain.action: replay ordinary requests with a host header built from the disclosed domain, trying the names the application's own vocabulary suggests
chain.why: the same port serves a completely different application once the host matches, and that application holds the vulnerable parameter

chain.action: point the hidden application's url parameter back at the header-mirroring endpoint on the loopback interface
chain.why: the server-side fetcher attaches a secret header to its own outbound request, and the mirror prints that header back in the response

first_confirming_probe.request: request the reflecting endpoint using the older protocol version with an empty host header, and compare the reflected host with the one returned by an ordinary request
first_confirming_probe.expected: the reflected host is an internal domain name rather than the address that was dialled
first_confirming_probe.falsifier: the reflected host is unchanged, or the proxy rejects the request outright

blast_radius: read-only. Every step is a GET, and the server-side fetch should be pointed only at the challenge's own loopback services. Do not aim the url parameter at anything outside the supplied instance, and do not use it as a general relay.

verification.evidence: the flag was returned inline by the live target as the value of the key field in the JSON the mirroring endpoint produced for the server-side fetch

reuse_when: a proxy-fronted target reflects the host header anywhere in a response
an application exposes both a url-fetching parameter and an endpoint that echoes request metadata
a site presents as static yet the challenge clearly expects a dynamic surface
known_traps: the loopback target must be addressed by the name the application expects: an address literal made the fetcher fail with an invalid status code error, while the name on the same port succeeded
the proxy normalises dot-dot segments before choosing a location, so traversal from the proxied prefix falls back to the static root instead of reaching another backend path
combining a content length with a chunked encoding is rejected by the proxy, so smuggling is not the way into the unproxied backend routes
the reflecting endpoint looks like a harmless debug route; its real value is that it prints credentials attached by a server-side fetcher
